Stellenbosch Art Heist

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Art Collectors and dealers weave a complex matric of high value property that changes hands in private deals and public auctions and hangs on the walls of the super rich. It’s like a secret society of who knows and owns what, and is very effective way of hiding money from the tax man. But seldom are theft charges laid against art dealers. But Lizahn Boonzaier takes no prisoners- she is determined to expose an R18 million rand art heist that’s been playing out in Stellenbosch for the last 20 years.

Summary:
Johan Coetzee is a well know art dealer and gallery owner on Stellenbosch main road, the hub of art collectors in South Africa. He’s known for giving you a good price for your art and pays up on the first sale, but after that you will struggle to get your money out of him. He pays people off in dribs and drabs. He’s been doing this for the last 20 years. Up until now he has got away with it because people are embarrassed to have been caught out and don’t want to expose a world where high value art moves around in private sales and confidentially. They also don’t want to sully their own reputations. When Johan runs out of cash he sells off other peoples valuable works of art very cheaply to the extremely wealthy in Stellenbosch just to get liquid again or to settle debts

Further information:
Lizahn Boonzaier niece of the famous Gregoire Boonzaier is no convention player- robbed of her art once she was not going to settle for Johan’s lies and obfuscation. Her former husband had stolen her art collection during a divorcee settlement and she had spent 6 years reclaiming it through court orders. She has two art collections. Johan had asked if she would bring her art from Pretoria to hang in his gallery during “Woordfees” in 3 March in 2018- a well know literary and art event held annually in Stellenbosch . She hung 29 Oil and pastel works and 69 Water colours. Johan sold 9 pieces for which she was paid except for a Pieter van der Westhuisen which was R150 000.
After months of trying to get her money out of Johan Lucien went to remove her art in August 2018 but 10 paintings were missing and ever since then she has been hunting for them. Lucien has had buyers for her art but she cannot get it back from Coetzee. Johan says they have gone and he will pay her. She filed theft charges at the Stellenbosch police station in September 2018. In December 2018 Johan was liquidated but he continued to trade and paid her out 3 further amounts from his gallery account. Coetzee owes her R600 000 in art and she is determined to get it back
Instead of joining the civil liquidation case losing good money after bad she is determined to pursue the criminal charges and forcing the police to take action. In early May the Paarl magistrate Orange Enslin issued a search and seize on Johan Coetzee and local billionaire Denis Zetler. They found nothing of value in the gallery but seized the art log book which revealed that Zetler had removed paintings against a R1.6 million debt which Coetzee had not settled. But the police were too frightened of Denis Zetler to force their way onto his property when the staff told him he was away.
And she is not alone. Adolf Van Coller a well-known art Dealer from George was caught in a similar fashion. Johan Coetzee contacted him saying he had several buyers and would Adolf bring his collection of Martin Botha’s for the 2019 Woordfees”. He delivered 10 works on consignment. Adolf had no idea that Coetzee had already been sequestrated in both his personal and gallery accounts. Coetzee sold an Eric Laubsher for R150 000. Once again Coetzee didn’t pay up and when he arrived to collect his works he found Zetler had removed 5 Martin Botha’s. He filed theft charges against both Zetler and Coetzee. But as Coetzee is already sequestrated he has no claim against the estate. Zetler returned 4 of the Martin Botha’s but is holding on to the 5th.
Lucien Boonzaier grandson of Gregoire Boonzaier and has R1.6 million rands worth of art missing. He has been paid out some money but he has been trying for 5 years to get his art or his money out of Johan Coetzee.
This is an R18 million art heist and it’s rocking the art world in South Africa. Johan Coetzee has not only devalued South African art by selling it off to who will ever buy it at whatever price he can get as his wheeling and dealings catch up with him he has also sold two fake Peter Clarks to Patrick Halliday a British art collector. This case is being fought in the high court currently.
But it’s all caught up with Johan Coetzee. The theft charges have gone viral. The missing art is registered on the international art theft Artinsure website. He’s been liquidated; the landlord locked the doors to the gallery and is evicting him with 6 months of outstanding rent. The police are looking for him. But will Adolf, Lucien and Lizahn ever see their art again? They have registered their claim against his estate but liquidation never compensates peole for the full value of what they have lost. Lucien wants her art pieces so she can move on with her life and she is not going to walk away from R600 000. We follow her on her quest to get answers from the police, Johan and possibly Dennis Zetler

Script:


Script: Art collector Lizahn Boonzaier is a woman on a mission, she has been hunting for her paintings worth nearly R600 thousand for the last 9 months, walking the streets of Stellenbosch trying to find answers from the art dealers in town
Lizahn “He is the art world in Stellenbosch it seems because nobody wants to talk about it and it's just been a really horrendous awful business ……
Link: The dealer in question is Johan Coetzee who has traded in art for many decades and has owned this well-known gallery on the high Street for the past 14 years
Script: He’s a well established figure and a cornerstone of the Stellenbosch art world.
Lizahn has an extensive art collection so when Johan Coetzee contacted her, she thought it was a secure way to sell some of her investment art
Lizahn “On the 3rd of March last year I gave him over 90 works to sell, so I basically filled his whole gallery for him.
Script: Although Lizahn received the first payment for 15 paintings, she was then given the runaround for months on end. Finally she returned to Stellenbosch to collect the outstanding paintings, but 7 were missing.
lizahn “ I walked in the 1st of August. [03:11:49] I saw my paintings was still against the wall. He was busy with a client. He asked me to come back eventually Phone calls, coming back, trying to uplift my stock, I walked in the Friday again and I saw my art was gone. Seven paintings disappeared.
Derek “So the obvious question is where are they.
lizahn “ I would really like to know where they are. Mr Coetzee says they have gone… I've heard on the streets that my art might be in houses in Israel.
Link “This is the hub of Stellenbosch Art District it's where you can expect to pick up one of the South African masters like a Tinus De Jonge, Maggie Laubscher or a Gregoire Boonzaier. It’s where some of our most valuable artworks change hands
Script: Art is an investment, traded through private dealers or on auction. Top South African art ranges between R700 000 to R52 Million. It’s a discrete world, where collectors and dealers weave an intricate network, it’s all about knowing who is collecting what, and how much they are prepared to pay for it. Dealers essentially are the middle person, protecting the identity of buyer and seller, but it’s unregulated, and largely works on a trust basis.
Script: In January this year Johan Coetzee contacted art dealer Adolph Van Coller, saying he had a prime opportunity to sell his art
adolph [04:31:31] he asked whether I would be prepared to provide him with some stock some consignment stock. [04:31:50] I was aware of the fact that he had been running a gallery for a long time with on the face of it was an apparent success because he kept going for a long time and I then sent him a number of works.
Script: Coetzee sold one of the paintings for R150 000 but Adolph never saw his money
Adolph” He immediately started giving me the runaround. There was lots of excuses and payment never materialized.
Script: For the past 5 years, Johan Coetzee has owed Lucien Boonzaier R185 000 for the art he sold painted by his famous grandfather Gregoire Boonziare
[04:02:43]He creates a work with soul and passion and you know it's it's being prostituted.
Script: Gregoire Boonzaier is considered to be one of the great 20th century South African masters, he was a prolific artist right up until his death at 96, and most famous for his District 6 oils. His paintings have been known to fetch up to a million rand
lucien [04:03:52] as a child I used to go with my grandfather when he used to go and paint out in the field. You know and I mean those are very fond memories. [04:02:14] You know that that he came from humble beginnings. And built himself up
Script: Despite the outstanding debt owing to Lucien, Johan Coetzee called him again last year and offered him another attractive deal
Lucien 03:45:26 He phoned me in June….and said he's got a client interested in Gregoire do I have anything. And I said yes I've got a beautiful Gregoire but we need to discuss your debt….
Script: Coetzee took 9 Boonzaier paintings and sold 5 of them way below value and has never paid Lucien a cent. The Boonzaier family are R1.8 million rand out of pocket, and have only been able to retrieve 4 of their paintings from the gallery
Derek [03:55:35] I take it that all of your family are angry to say the least.
Lucien [03:55:41] Of course. It's I mean it affects us all. And yes as you know this left a very bitter taste in my mouth. You know and I mean where do we stand. As the victim. I mean that's I'm left out in the cold. You know it's like I have no to go. You know every avenue we've tried a door get shut in our face.
Derek [04:38:03] So what are you down the tubes for.
Adolph [04:38:05] For two hundred and thirty thousand at this at this point in time. [04:44:03] You know I think the art world is uh an unregulated industry as it is. There is a lot of room for things like this to happen and I think that the annoying thing is the silence that comes along with something like that. [04:44:20] ….I've spoken to on an informal basis. In the UK in Argentina in Gansbaai in Pretoria in Cape Town they're all over the show but they're not always willing to talk.
Link 05 07 06 There is a twist in the tail of the missing art works. Denis Zetler prominent figure and strawberry farmer in Stellenbosch says Johan Coetzee owes him a substantial amount of money so when he could see the writing on the wall he took more than 20 paintings from the gallery, the question is who do they actually belong to?
Zetler [06:02:50] I got to Coetzee and he said I will pay you but I will give you paintings for securities so long and you must just sign for it. So he gave me paintings for security and I that's what I took and he said You said you keep this until I give you the money and then. Then you have to give the paintings back. If I give you the money
Script: We asked Zetler where the paintings were now
Zetler [06:07:44] I took it overseas I gave it to families overseas.
Script: But those artworks belong to other people who have handed them over on consignment and it was thanks to Lizahns detective work that Adolf discovered 5 of the 20 paintings given to Zetler were his.
Lizahn [03:16:58] … Johan Coetzee in his own handwriting he had stated that he had taken two David Bothas and a Karl Bogner to Mr Zetlers house on the 6th of March this year
Script: Initially Zetler co-operated handing back 4 of the 5 paintings in exchange for other art from Coetzee, but Adolf alleges he’s holding on his last painting
Zetler [06:09:49] he said I had five these paintings but I could only find four I had and I gave the four go back. Zetler [06:04:31] I haven't got that painting. Everybody says I've got the painting
Script: Zetler says that Coetzee statement given to Adolph that he took 5 paintings out the gallery without permission, is a lie
Link: 05 37 02 13 After months of trying to pin him down Lucien, Adolph and Lizahn pressed charges of theft against Johan Coetzee and Adolf also pressed charges of theft and fraud against Denis Zetler
Script: It took 8 months of Lizahns persistent badgering of the police before they issued a search and seize on Zetler and Coetzee
02 12 03 11 Lizahn I am on my way to do a search and seize on Mr Zetlers house, last time I was there he wasn’t available so we are doing it this morning and hopefully I will be able to find some of my art there
Script: The search was fruitless, and Lizahn is still none the wiser as to where her and Adolph missing paintings have gone.
Adolph [04:39:20] if you have sufficient evidence as a state prosecutor to authorise a search and seizure document …in both the case of Johan Coetzee and Dennis Zetler then surely there is a proper premafika case to follow up
Script: The Western Cape Police responded by saying the theft charges are under investigation and being perused by the Senior State Prosecutor and his decision is awaited.
Script: It was the end of an era and a very public exposure of the double deals of this cornerstone of the art establishment, after 6 months in arrears with his rent, the landlord finally evicted him
Cellphone Liz 0.12 he’s been telling me tomorrow tomorrow tomorrow but tomorrow never comes
Script: Returning in the morning, we hoped to catch Johan clearing out the shop, but he had returned later that night and stripped it. And as Lizahn predicted, more victims kept pitching up. Ane Wessels had an appointment with Johan to collect 15 of her father’s paintings worth R2.6 million
Ane My dad is devastated,he's lost a lot of money and he's been collecting art all his life, and just for it to be taken like this, it’s ridiculous. It was purely here so Johan could exhibit the art. And then if someone would be interested. he would. Bring that person to my dad to negotiate the sale. And when the sale goes through Johan would get commission. Johan said you know I could come and pick it up. But here I am and the art galleries closed.
Script: After months of dodging Lizahn phone calls, Johan finally her call back while we were talking to her, but said pushed for time
Upsound Lizahn” Morning Johan how are you- Johan”I will phone you back I just need a bit longer- Johan I don’t have time for your games
Johan “No Lizahn I called you yesterday I will call you back I must just finish with a very important thing
Lizahn “Johan seeing that we are here, I had no other option but to go to Carte Blanche and Mr Derek Watts is here with me he just wants to ask you a question
Morning Johan Derek Watts from Carte Blanche… he has gone
Script: Much to everyone’s shock Johan was liquidated and sequestrated in November last year which he failed to reveal, so anyone trading with him this year has absolutely no claim against his estate
Derek [04:45:08] When you handed over the paintings on consignment did you know that you Johan Coetzee had already been sequestrated.
Adolph [04:45:16] I had no clue. …..No person in his right mind would give consignment stock of over 500000 rand to a liquidated business, never.
Link 05 03 38 05 This insolvency sign says it all. His home in Somerset West is up for auction it seems as things have finally caught up with the Gallery owner after years of alleged double dealings
04 57 41 23 Lizahn at front door “Johan ek will regtig will met jou praat. Johan You don’t have an appointment. No Johan .04 57 58 14 Nothing- I don’t have an appointment with him I need an appointment with a man who owes me almost R600 000 are you kidding me.
Derek 04 59 11 15 Lizahn Johan won’t speak to you and he certainly won’t speak to us what’s the next step
Lizahn “ its theft I want my art back, I want to know where it is, the art has got no value to the person who has got it it’s listed as stolen

Zetler [06:02:50] I got to Coetzee and he said I will pay you but I will give you paintings for securities so long and you must just sign for it. So he gave me paintings for security and I that's what I took and he said You said you keep this until I give you the money and then. Then you have to give the paintings back. If I give you the money Script: We asked Zetler where the paintings were now Zetler [06:07:44] I took it overseas I gave it to families overseas. Script: But those artworks belong to other people who have handed them over on consignment and it was thanks to Lizahns detective work that Adolf discovered 5 of the 20 paintings given to Zetler were his. Lizahn [03:16:58] … Johan Coetzee in his own handwriting he had stated that he had taken two David Bothas and a Karl Bogner to Mr Zetlers house on the 6th of March this year Script: Initially Zetler co-operated handing back 4 of the 5 paintings in exchange for other art from Coetzee, but Adolf alleges he’s holding on his last painting Zetler [06:09:49] he said I had five these paintings but I could only find four I had and I gave the four go back. Zetler [06:04:31] I haven't got that painting. Everybody says I've got the painting Script: Zetler says that Coetzee statement given to Adolph that he took 5 paintings out the gallery without permission, is a lie Link: 05 37 02 13 After months of trying to pin him down Lucien, Adolph and Lizahn pressed charges of theft against Johan Coetzee and Adolf also pressed charges of theft and fraud against Denis Zetler Script: It took 8 months of Lizahns persistent badgering of the police before they issued a search and seize on Zetler and Coetzee 02 12 03 11 Lizahn I am on my way to do a search and seize on Mr Zetlers house, last time I was there he wasn’t available so we are doing it this morning and hopefully I will be able to find some of my art there Script: The search was fruitless, and Lizahn is still none the wiser as to where her and Adolph missing paintings have gone. Adolph [04:39:20] if you have sufficient evidence as a state prosecutor to authorise a search and seizure document …in both the case of Johan Coetzee and Dennis Zetler then surely there is a proper premafika case to follow up Script: The Western Cape Police responded by saying the theft charges are under investigation and being perused by the Senior State Prosecutor and his decision is awaited. Script: It was the end of an era and a very public exposure of the double deals of this cornerstone of the art establishment, after 6 months in arrears with his rent, the landlord finally evicted him Cellphone Liz 0.12 he’s been telling me tomorrow tomorrow tomorrow but tomorrow never comes Script: Returning in the morning, we hoped to catch Johan clearing out the shop, but he had returned later that night and stripped it. And as Lizahn predicted, more victims kept pitching up. Ane Wessels had an appointment with Johan to collect 15 of her father’s paintings worth R2.6 million Ane My dad is devastated,he's lost a lot of money and he's been collecting art all his life, and just for it to be taken like this, it’s ridiculous. It was purely here so Johan could exhibit the art. And then if someone would be interested. he would. Bring that person to my dad to negotiate the sale. And when the sale goes through Johan would get commission. Johan said you know I could come and pick it up. But here I am and the art galleries closed. metadata.Unique Selling Point: Art Collectors and dealers weave a complex matric of high value property that changes hands in private deals and public auctions and hangs on the walls of the super rich. It’s like a secret society of who knows and owns what, and is very effective way of hiding money from the tax man. But seldom are theft charges laid against art dealers. But Lizahn Boonzaier takes no prisoners- she is determined to expose an R18 million rand art heist that’s been playing out in Stellenbosch for the last 20 years.
metadata.Summary: Johan Coetzee is a well know art dealer and gallery owner on Stellenbosch main road, the hub of art collectors in South Africa. He’s known for giving you a good price for your art and pays up on the first sale, but after that you will struggle to get your money out of him. He pays people off in dribs and drabs. He’s been doing this for the last 20 years. Up until now he has got away with it because people are embarrassed to have been caught out and don’t want to expose a world where high value art moves around in private sales and confidentially. They also don’t want to sully their own reputations. When Johan runs out of cash he sells off other peoples valuable works of art very cheaply to the extremely wealthy in Stellenbosch just to get liquid again or to settle debts
metadata.Further information: Lizahn Boonzaier niece of the famous Gregoire Boonzaier is no convention player- robbed of her art once she was not going to settle for Johan’s lies and obfuscation. Her former husband had stolen her art collection during a divorcee settlement and she had spent 6 years reclaiming it through court orders. She has two art collections. Johan had asked if she would bring her art from Pretoria to hang in his gallery during “Woordfees” in 3 March in 2018- a well know literary and art event held annually in Stellenbosch . She hung 29 Oil and pastel works and 69 Water colours. Johan sold 9 pieces for which she was paid except for a Pieter van der Westhuisen which was R150 000. After months of trying to get her money out of Johan Lucien went to remove her art in August 2018 but 10 paintings were missing and ever since then she has been hunting for them. Lucien has had buyers for her art but she cannot get it back from Coetzee. Johan says they have gone and he will pay her. She filed theft charges at the Stellenbosch police station in September 2018. In December 2018 Johan was liquidated but he continued to trade and paid her out 3 further amounts from his gallery account. Coetzee owes her R600 000 in art and she is determined to get it back Instead of joining the civil liquidation case losing good money after bad she is determined to pursue the criminal charges and forcing the police to take action. In early May the Paarl magistrate Orange Enslin issued a search and seize on Johan Coetzee and local billionaire Denis Zetler. They found nothing of value in the gallery but seized the art log book which revealed that Zetler had removed paintings against a R1.6 million debt which Coetzee had not settled. But the police were too frightened of Denis Zetler to force their way onto his property when the staff told him he was away. And she is not alone. Adolf Van Coller a well-known art Dealer from George was caught in a similar fashion. Johan Coetzee contacted him saying he had several buyers and would Adolf bring his collection of Martin Botha’s for the 2019 Woordfees”. He delivered 10 works on consignment. Adolf had no idea that Coetzee had already been sequestrated in both his personal and gallery accounts. Coetzee sold an Eric Laubsher for R150 000. Once again Coetzee didn’t pay up and when he arrived to collect his works he found Zetler had removed 5 Martin Botha’s. He filed theft charges against both Zetler and Coetzee. But as Coetzee is already sequestrated he has no claim against the estate. Zetler returned 4 of the Martin Botha’s but is holding on to the 5th. Lucien Boonzaier grandson of Gregoire Boonzaier and has R1.6 million rands worth of art missing. He has been paid out some money but he has been trying for 5 years to get his art or his money out of Johan Coetzee. This is an R18 million art heist and it’s rocking the art world in South Africa. Johan Coetzee has not only devalued South African art by selling it off to who will ever buy it at whatever price he can get as his wheeling and dealings catch up with him he has also sold two fake Peter Clarks to Patrick Halliday a British art collector. This case is being fought in the high court currently. But it’s all caught up with Johan Coetzee. The theft charges have gone viral. The missing art is registered on the international art theft Artinsure website. He’s been liquidated; the landlord locked the doors to the gallery and is evicting him with 6 months of outstanding rent. The police are looking for him. But will Adolf, Lucien and Lizahn ever see their art again? They have registered their claim against his estate but liquidation never compensates peole for the full value of what they have lost. Lucien wants her art pieces so she can move on with her life and she is not going to walk away from R600 000. We follow her on her quest to get answers from the police, Johan and possibly Dennis Zetler
